content.intro: {state} charges {stateRate} sales tax on the price of a vehicle bought from a dealer, less your trade-in. Registration lasts two years and depends on weight, and your city or town bills a yearly excise tax.

howItWorks.text: The sales tax is {stateRate} of the purchase price minus trade-in and other allowances for a dealer sale of a passenger vehicle.
A private sale is taxed on the greater of the book value or the sale price for newer vehicles.
Registration fees follow the vehicle's weight, and a state transportation surcharge is added for each year.

faq.q: Does a trade-in lower the sales tax in Rhode Island?
faq.text: Yes for a dealer sale of a passenger vehicle, the tax is figured on the price minus the trade-in and other allowances.
A renewal covers two years, and the weight-based fee is charged for the full term.
